Every reform follows the same pattern: a crisis triggers a proposal → the captured system weakens it during implementation → the weakened reform fails to produce accountability → the next crisis triggers the next proposal → repeat.

The 13-layer architecture is designed to absorb reform attempts without changing outcomes. That is why citizen action and class actions bypass the system entirely — because reform from within is structurally impossible.
